title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Past $4.56 sales: 195 (x0.94), 119 (x0.57); median 157, 25% below baseline. Price increase likely reduces demand. Adjusted from 1.0 to 0.88.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween has a noise-adjusted historical effect of x1.0, so no uplift. The 5.1% price increase to $4.56 is a strong headwind. Past 30% off promo (2024-10-28) saw only x0.95 vs baseline, suggesting price sensitivity. The current price is higher than any past promotion, and recent weeks at $4.56 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) sold 195 and 119 units—below baseline. Heatwave may boost demand slightly, but no evidence supports that. No promotion, so no uplift. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends. Confidence is medium due to limited price effect data.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.6 - 290.2 | 10%-90%: 156.4 - 281.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
